canonical_statement: The supplementary package pertains to a systematic review and network meta-analysis comparing glucose-lowering medications for body weight and blood pressure outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes.
The appendix reports full electronic search strategies for MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase via Ovid, and CENTRAL/Cochrane sources, including randomized-trial filters.

The update flow identified 3,800 database records, removed 1,119 duplicates, screened 2,681 title/abstract records and 358 full texts, found 19 eligible reports representing 18 trials, and combined these with 406 trials from the initial review for 424 trials in the final systematic review and network meta-analysis.
The appendix reports estimated heterogeneity values of 1.1203 for body weight, 1.8278 for systolic blood pressure, and 0.1639 for diastolic blood pressure.
For body weight, 8/94 comparisons (8.51%) were identified as inconsistent; the design-by-treatment interaction model reported Q=150.68, df=111, p=0.01.
For systolic blood pressure, 2/82 comparisons (2.44%) were identified as inconsistent; the design-by-treatment interaction model reported Q=66.60, df=86, p=0.94.
For diastolic blood pressure, 4/81 comparisons (4.94%) were identified as inconsistent; the design-by-treatment interaction model reported Q=62.25, df=80, p=0.93.
Comparison-adjusted funnel plots are provided for change from baseline in body weight, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure.

In the drug-class network meta-analysis, Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors versus placebo yielded a mean difference of -0.39 (95% CI -0.82 to 0.04) for change in body weight; negative values favor the active treatment.
